claims.text: The hypothesis applies to CrFeCoNiX alloys in single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
Formation of a stable oxide layer is governed by competition between protective-scale growth and formation of less-protective oxides.
Cr2O3 and Al2O3 are protective oxide scales in the stated alloy and exposure regime.
FeO and NiO are less-protective oxides in the stated alloy and exposure regime.
The content of X strongly influences protective-scale formation.
Competition among oxide-growth pathways determines oxide-layer composition and structure.
Oxide-layer composition and structure determine its stability and coherence.
Increasing Al or Si content is predicted to produce a stable, coherent, slow-growing protective layer that persists above 900 °C in an oxidative or corrosive atmosphere.
Alloys described as having lower X content, exemplified by Mn-containing alloys, may undergo oxide cracking or spallation.
The proposed test systematically varies X content and measures oxide composition, structure, and stability after exposure above 900 °C.
